title: feat(plugin-timeline): declare `navigation` on object-timeline, by reference to the spec (objectui#8654)
body:
Fixes #8654
Clause-②: yes

`navigation` is now declared on the `object-timeline` block, by reference to the spec. This is the timeline arm of the objectui#8652 maintainer ruling (verbatim 「B」): declare the key on the platform element schema first, then mirror it here. The platform half shipped in `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0, the release this repo resolves: `ComponentPropsMap['object-timeline']` declares `navigation: NavigationConfigSchema.optional()`, and its docblock names it the spec half of that ruling, honoured standalone, with no enclosing view.

Dispatched by the `domain:spec @ objectui` seat (objectui#10217), session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01VhxTqosz7wn54ahqyxgERT`.

## Premises, re-measured on `origin/main` `cd5b19a7e` before the first edit

- **H1 holds; no edit there.** `ObjectTimelineBlockSchema` reads the spec row by reference in its `properties` bag. On the installed 17.5.0, `{ type: 'object-timeline', properties: { navigation: { mode: 'drawer' } } }` parses on `safeValidateSchema` and on `StrictAnyComponentSchema`. A bad `mode` is refused at `properties.navigation.mode` and a bogus member at `properties.navigation`, on both faces. A parse writes no default. `objectql.zod.ts` is untouched.
- **H2 confirmed, but its placement is falsified.** The TypeScript checker (`getPropertyOfType`, not a grep) reads `navigation` as NOT DECLARED on `ObjectTimelineProps['schema']` and on `TimelineSchema`; the read went through `(schema as any).navigation`. The same instrument's lit control is the reason this PR does not put the member on `TimelineSchema`: `objectName`, a member of the same spec row, reads DECLARED on the plugin-local half of `ObjectTimelineProps['schema']` and NOT DECLARED on `TimelineSchema`. A nonsense key reads not declared on both.
  - `TimelineSchema` is the presentational rail (`type: 'timeline'`). Its docblock calls its vocabulary disjoint from the object-bound one by design, and `TimelineRenderer` never reads `navigation`.
  - The spec declares `navigation` on the `object-timeline` row only and has no `timeline` component row. Declaring it on `TimelineSchema` would add the key to a face the spec does not declare it on (the dispatch's zone-1 ruling forbids that).
  - Measured: the strict face refuses `objectName` on `type: 'timeline'`. A `navigation` declared there could not build the `new_window` URL, which needs the object name.
  - objectui#8220 handled `filter` and `sort` on these same two tags the same way: registration `inputs` on both tags, `TimelineSchema` left alone.
  - ⇒ The member is declared on the object-bound half of `ObjectTimelineProps['schema']` in `plugin-timeline/src/ObjectTimeline.tsx`, beside `objectName`, `timeline`, `filter` and `sort`. That file is inside the claim. `@object-ui/types` is NOT changed: neither `data-display.ts` nor `zod/data-display.zod.ts` is touched, so this PR does not overlap the objectui#6152 round-5 region.
- **H3 confirmed.** Neither registration published `navigation`. The description was written from measurement on the real component, and it differs from the board's and the calendar's in two places, as listed under Acceptance notes.
- **H4 confirmed: the guard owes nothing here and cannot take a pin yet.** `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` books `object-timeline` in `UNJUDGED_SPEC_BLOCKS`, owed to objectui#11168 (it does not load the lazily registered block). Its assertion `every member pin names a key that is still array/object-armed on a covered block` would refuse a `MEMBER_PINS` entry for `object-timeline.navigation`. So that file is NOT edited. The pin file below names the block and the key, so the locator accepts it when slice 3 registers the entry.

## What changed

- `@object-ui/plugin-timeline`:
  - `ObjectTimelineProps['schema']` declares `navigation?: ViewNavigationConfig`, the spec's `NavigationConfig` type that `ObjectGridSchema`, `ObjectKanbanSchema` and `ObjectCalendarSchema` use. `ObjectTimeline` reads `schema.navigation` with no cast. The read still supplies no default (see Acceptance notes).
  - Both registrations, `object-timeline` and `view:timeline`, publish a `navigation` input typed `object`, with one shared description. Both tags carry it for the reason both carry `filter` and `sort`: `view:timeline` is the same renderer under a second tag. That is also the calendar precedent from PR objectui#11292 (`OBJECT_CALENDAR_INPUTS`, shared by `object-calendar` and `calendar`).
  - Docs (AGENTS.md #2): `README.md` and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-timeline.mdx` document the object-bound block's `properties` bag and its `navigation` key, member by member, with the three cases that open nothing.
- Changeset `.changeset/8654-timeline-navigation.md`: `@object-ui/plugin-timeline` minor (a widening). The fixed group moves together anyway.

### Pins

- `object-timeline-navigation-8654.test.tsx`:
  - the spec premise, read live from the installed spec: it declares the key, and it refuses a bad `mode` at `navigation.mode`;
  - on both validator faces, value-level: every mode parses, a bad `mode` is refused at `properties.navigation.mode`, a bogus member is refused, the retired `view` member is refused, and a parse writes no default;
  - the TS face: an `Equal` assertion, a `@ts-expect-error` bad-mode row, and a valid block that annotates with no cast;
  - both registrations: the input is declared as `object`, the html tier accepts the block and refuses a string by kind, and a control prop is still reported as unknown;
  - end to end through the real `SchemaRenderer` and registry, on both tags: an authored drawer block opens the record, and the same node without the key opens nothing.
- `timelineNavigationMembers-8654.test.tsx`, the member pin: every member through a real entry click on the real `ObjectTimeline`, `useNavigationOverlay` and overlay shell:
  - `drawer` (the lit control), `modal` and `popover` open the entry's record;
  - `none` opens nothing, and `preventNavigation` outranks an overlay mode;
  - `new_window` opens the record page in a new tab, and `openNewTab` does too, outranking both `page` and `drawer`;
  - `size` resolves through the bucket table, a deprecated `width` wins over `size`, and `auto` gives the unsized width;
  - a parent `onRowClick` outranks the whole key;
  - four warning rows hold the description to the truth: an absent key, `page`, a mode-less block and `split` each open nothing.

  - console: `registry-inputs-spec-parity`, `public-contract`, `public-block-binding-reach`, `timelineAxisRefusalReach-7070`, `filterContextTokensSweep-10666`, `pullToRefreshOwner-10105`;
  - types: `object-timeline-arm-10859-b3`, `object-kanban-calendar-navigation-8652`, `timeline-declared-keys`, `zod-mirror-parity`, `base-bind-declared`, `timeline-catalog-fixture-migrated`;
  - `navigationOverlayConsumers.onRowClickArity-9357`, `ObjectTree.schemaTyped-8655`, `registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859`, `catalog-gallery-render`, the list and view timeline-binding suites;
  - the script tests for component-surface-parity, designer-field-key-parity, handler-key-read-sites, prompt-component-keys, sdui-registration-pins, registry-bare-names and date-only-zone-pins.

  - `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:prompt-keys`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:registry-bare-names`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:spec-symbols`;

  - `check:readme-exports`, `check:doc-snippets` and `check:doc-examples`, each run after the doc-snippet build closure was built (the first `readme-exports` run reported a collapsed population on an unbuilt tree, which is not a verdict);
  - `check:sdui-registration-pins` and `check:eager-closure`, each run after a full console build (the first console build stopped on an unbuilt `@object-ui/plugin-tree`, which is a prerequisite miss, not a verdict).
- Lint, as a declared narrowing:
  - `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 4 changed TS files reports 4 files and 0 errors.
  - Warnings against the base blobs: `ObjectTimeline.tsx` 28 to 27 (the removed cast) and `index.tsx` 5 to 5. The new contract pin carries 1, the deliberate `any` in its `Equal` control.
  - `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions` / `projectService`). None of the 10 rule sources under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem; as a control, 9 of them contain `context.report`. So this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.

### Ablations, each committed first, run through `ablation-replace.mjs`, and restored to `HEAD`

Each ablation was proven landed by anchor count and blob change. Each restore was proven by blob equals `HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`, and the tree was clean afterwards.

- **TS member removed** (renamed away, so the import stays used): `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exits 2, with TS2344 on the `Equal` assertion and TS2578 (unused `@ts-expect-error`) on the bad-mode row. This was the predicted direction.
- **Renderer read ignores the authored key** (`navigation: undefined`): 11 failed and 27 passed. The 11 are exactly the rows where a click opens something: 9 member rows and the 2 end-to-end drawer rows. Every "opens nothing" row and the parent-handler row stayed green. ⚠️ The count pre-registered before the run was 12, a miscount by me; enumerating the "opens something" rows gives 11.
- **`object-timeline` registration row removed** (the `view:timeline` row kept): 2 failed and 20 passed, as predicted. The failures were the declared-as-object row and the html-tier row for that tag. The first attempt was a no-op, which the tool refused before running anything: the replacement was a suffix of the anchor, so its count could not rise. It was re-anchored and re-run.
- The validator face was not ablated, because this PR does not change it. Its rows pin the existing by-reference reading (objectui#10859 batch 3).

## Acceptance notes

- ⚠️ **Three cases open nothing on a standalone timeline.** All three are measured on the real component. The description, the docs and four pin rows state them. They are not changed here.
  - An **absent key** opens nothing. Unlike `ObjectKanban` and `ObjectCalendar`, `ObjectTimeline` supplies no `?? { mode: 'drawer' }` default, so the hook resolves the spec's `page`.
  - `page`, and a block written without `mode`, open nothing. This is the objectui#11293 family, and the timeline is a third site of it.
  - `split` opens nothing. The timeline hands `NavigationOverlay` no `mainContent`, and the split shell returns nothing without it. The board, the calendar, the gantt and the grid all pass it. This is reported to the seat as a finding.
- `onItemClick` fires twice per entry click when it is the only host handler. `ObjectTimeline` hands `onRowClick ?? onItemClick` to the hook, which calls it. The composed `onItemClick` then calls `onItemClick` again after `navigation.handleClick`. This was measured once by a probe (two calls, with 2 and 1 arguments). No in-repo producer passes `onItemClick` to `ObjectTimeline`. Not pinned. Carrier: none.
- The strict authoring face refuses `objectName` on `type: 'timeline'`, while the `view:timeline` registration marks it `required: true`. That is pre-existing and was observed while choosing the TS face. It is not measured through a public door. Carrier: none.
- Overlap: PR objectui#11312 (objectui#11117) is in `objectql.zod.ts`, which this PR does not touch. objectui#6152 round 5 is in `data-display.ts` / `zod/data-display.zod.ts`, which this PR does not touch either. `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` is not edited.
